title: Healthcare Reform Remains a Major Debate Before Midterm Elections
subtitle: Democrats are divided on how to fix rising costs and insurance issues as voters prepare for November.

summary.en: Healthcare reform is a top priority for voters as the midterm elections approach. Progressive Democrats are strongly advocating for a 'Medicare for All' system to provide universal coverage. Centrist Democrats argue that smaller, step-by-step changes are more realistic and effective. Both sides agree that current costs are too high and need to be addressed. The party must now decide on a unified path forward to attract voters.
summary.zh: 隨著期中選舉臨近，醫療保健改革成為選民的首要考量。進步派民主黨人強烈主張實施「全民醫療保險」制度以提供全面覆蓋。中間派民主黨人則認為，小規模的逐步改革更為務實且有效。雙方皆同意目前的成本過高，必須加以解決。該黨現在必須決定一條統一的前進道路，以吸引選民。

paragraphs.en: As the November midterm elections draw closer, the debate over how to fix the American healthcare system has become a central point of tension within the Democratic Party. While all members agree that the current system is too expensive and difficult for many families, they remain deeply divided on the best way to make improvements.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著十一月期中選舉日益臨近，關於如何改善美國醫療保健體系的辯論，已成為民主黨內部的核心緊張點。儘管所有成員都同意目前的體系過於昂貴，且對許多家庭而言難以負擔，但對於採取何種最佳方式進行改善，黨內仍存在嚴重分歧。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Health, this divide was highlighted at a recent meeting in San Francisco. Over 1,500 unionized nurses gathered to show their support for 'Medicare for All.' This is a proposal to create a single, government-run health insurance program for every person in the country, replacing the current mix of private and public insurance. Supporters, including Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, argue that in a wealthy nation, no one should suffer because they cannot afford medical care. For these advocates, the plan is a necessary step to stop unnecessary illnesses and high costs.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，這項分歧在近期於舊金山舉行的一場會議中顯露無遺。超過一千五百名工會護理師齊聚一堂，表達對「全民醫療保險」（Medicare for All）的支持。這項提案旨在建立一個由政府營運的單一健康保險計畫，涵蓋全國每一位民眾，以取代目前混合私人與公共保險的現狀。支持者包括民主黨參議院提名人艾爾薩耶德（Abdul El-Sayed），他們主張在一個富裕的國家，不應有人因為負擔不起醫療費用而受苦。對這些倡議者而言，這項計畫是阻止不必要疾病與高昂成本的必要手段。

paragraphs.en: However, not all Democrats agree that this is the right approach. Centrist members of the party worry that 'Medicare for All' is too radical and could hurt the party's chances with moderate voters. Gabe Horwitz, a senior official at the centrist group Third Way, described the plan as an 'unattainable albatross,' meaning it is a heavy burden that is impossible to achieve. Instead, these centrists prefer 'incremental reform'—a series of small, step-by-step changes that build upon the existing Affordable Care Act (ACA), a law passed during the Obama administration to expand insurance access.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，並非所有民主黨人都認為這是正確的途徑。黨內的溫和派成員擔心「全民醫療保險」過於激進，可能會損害該黨爭取中間選民的機會。中間派團體「第三條路」（Third Way）的資深官員霍維茲（Gabe Horwitz）將此計畫形容為「無法實現的沉重負擔」，意指這是一個不可能達成且會拖累黨的包袱。相反地，這些中間派傾向於「漸進式改革」，即一系列基於現行《平價醫療法案》（ACA）的小規模、逐步調整；該法案是在歐巴馬政府時期通過，旨在擴大保險覆蓋範圍。

paragraphs.en: These centrist proposals include creating a 'public option,' which is a government-sponsored health insurance plan that people could choose to buy. They also suggest providing more government subsidies—financial help from the government—to insurance companies to lower the costs for everyday people. According to a memo sent to House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic Caucus holds a wide variety of views on how to reach the goal of universal coverage, ranging from the total overhaul of Medicare for All to these more limited, gradual changes.
paragraphs.zh: 這些中間派的提案包括建立「公共選項」，即一種民眾可以選擇購買的政府資助健康保險計畫。他們也建議提供更多政府補貼——即來自政府的財務援助——給保險公司，以降低一般民眾的成本。根據一份發送給眾議院少數黨領袖傑福瑞斯（Hakeem Jeffries）的備忘錄，民主黨黨團對於如何達成全民覆蓋目標持有廣泛且不同的觀點，從全面改革的「全民醫療保險」到這些更為有限、漸進的變革皆包含在內。

paragraphs.en: Despite these internal disagreements, the Democratic Party remains united in its opposition to recent Republican-led legislation. Democrats have strongly criticized the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act,' which was supported by Donald Trump. The party refers to this as the 'big, ugly bill' because it includes $1 trillion in healthcare cuts. According to reports cited by The Guardian Health, experts expect this legislation will cause an additional 16 million people to lose their health insurance by 2034.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管存在這些內部歧見，民主黨在反對近期由共和黨主導的立法上仍保持團結。民主黨人強烈批評由川普（Donald Trump）支持的《一項美好大法案》（One Big Beautiful Bill Act）。該黨將其稱為「醜陋的大法案」，因為其中包含了高達一兆美元的醫療保健預算削減。根據《衛報健康》引述的報告，專家預計這項立法將導致到二〇三四年時，額外有一千六百萬人失去健康保險。

paragraphs.en: For many voters, the central question is which path will actually lower their monthly bills and improve their access to doctors. While the party’s left wing sees Medicare for All as the only way to solve the problem, centrists argue that the party must focus on practical solutions that can pass in Congress. As Horwitz noted, there is complete agreement on the goals—to get everyone insured and lower costs—but there is no agreement on the means, or the specific methods, to get there.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多選民而言，核心問題在於哪條路徑能真正降低他們的每月帳單並改善就醫管道。雖然該黨的左派將「全民醫療保險」視為解決問題的唯一途徑，但中間派則主張，該黨必須專注於能在國會通過的務實解決方案。正如霍維茲所指出的，雙方在目標上完全一致——即讓所有人獲得保險並降低成本——但在達成目標的手段或具體方法上，卻毫無共識。

paragraphs.en: As the election date nears, this debate will likely continue to shape the party's message. Progressive candidates are finding success in primary elections by championing bold reforms, which puts pressure on the party leadership to address the concerns of their base. At the same time, the need to win over moderate voters keeps the focus on more careful, measured policies. Whether the party can present a unified front on healthcare remains to be seen, but the outcome of this debate will have a lasting impact on millions of Americans who are currently struggling with the high price of staying healthy.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著選舉日逼近，這場辯論很可能會持續形塑該黨的訊息。進步派候選人在初選中透過倡導大膽改革取得成功，這對黨領導層構成了必須回應基層訴求的壓力。與此同時，爭取中間選民的需求，也讓焦點持續放在更謹慎、審慎的政策上。民主黨能否在醫療保健議題上展現統一陣線仍有待觀察，但這場辯論的結果，將對數百萬目前正為維持健康的高昂代價而掙扎的美國人，產生深遠的影響。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To approach in time; to get nearer to a specific event.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見 draw 作「畫畫」或「拉」解，這裡指時間的推移。文中：As the November midterm elections draw closer, the debate over how to fix the American healthcare system has become a central point of tension within the Democratic Party.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The core group of supporters or voters of a political party.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「底部」或「基地」，這裡指政黨最忠實的支持群體。文中：Progressive candidates are finding success in primary elections by championing bold reforms, which puts pressure on the party leadership to address the concerns of their base.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A united group or appearance presented to the public.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （團體呈現出的）一致立場、陣線。

previousArticles.summaryEn: Healthcare remains a central topic for voters as the midterm elections draw near. Progressive Democrats are pushing for 'Medicare for All' to ensure universal coverage. Meanwhile, centrist Democrats prefer smaller, step-by-step reforms to the current system. President Donald Trump has announced new $90 payments for seniors to help with Medicare costs. These competing approaches highlight the deep divide in how the U.S. should manage health insurance and affordability.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary concern regarding the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act' supported by Donald Trump?

options.A: It would force all citizens to switch to private insurance plans.
options.B: It is projected to result in 16 million people losing their health insurance by 2034.
options.C: It would replace the Affordable Care Act with a government-run single-payer system.
options.D: It lacks support from the Democratic Caucus due to its focus on 'incremental reform'.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第五段明確指出，根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）引用的報告，專家預計該法案將導致到 2034 年時，額外有 1,600 萬人失去醫療保險。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章未提及該法案強制轉換保險；選項 C 錯誤，因為該法案並非建立單一付款人制度；選項 D 錯誤，因為該法案是共和黨主導，並非民主黨黨團的漸進式改革提案。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why might Democratic party leaders feel pressured as the midterm elections approach?

options.A: They must reconcile the demand for bold, progressive reforms with the need to attract moderate voters.
options.B: They are worried that the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act' will actually improve healthcare access.
options.C: They are struggling to find enough funding to support the 'public option' proposal.
options.D: They have failed to agree on the core goals of lowering costs and increasing insurance coverage.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文章最後一段提到，進步派候選人在初選中因支持大膽改革而成功，這對領導層構成了壓力；同時，為了贏得中間選民，黨內又必須聚焦於謹慎、審慎的政策。這顯示領導層必須在兩者之間取得平衡。選項 B 與文章事實相反；選項 C 文章未提及資金不足問題；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章第六段明確表示黨內對於「目標」（降低成本與全民保險）是有共識的，分歧僅在於「手段」。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, what does Gabe Horwitz mean when he describes 'Medicare for All' as an 'unattainable albatross'?

options.A: It is a popular policy that is too expensive to implement immediately.
options.B: It is a heavy, burdensome concept that is impossible to realize.
options.C: It is a rare and beautiful idea that needs more public support.
options.D: It is a strategic plan designed to divide the Republican Party.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章在第三段括號中直接解釋了 'unattainable albatross' 的含義，即「一個沉重的負擔，且是不可能實現的」。'Albatross' 在文學中常指沉重的負擔（源自《古舟子詠》）。選項 A 雖然提到昂貴，但未捕捉到「無法實現」的核心意涵；選項 C 將 'beautiful' 誤解為字面意思，忽略了這是一個貶義的比喻；選項 D 與文意無關。

quiz.question: Which of the following best summarizes the central theme of the article?

options.A: The Democratic Party is fully unified in its support for the Affordable Care Act.
options.B: Medicare for All is the only viable solution to the American healthcare crisis.
options.C: The Democratic Party faces internal conflict regarding the best strategy to reform the healthcare system.
options.D: Republican-led healthcare legislation is the only topic being debated in the upcoming midterm elections.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文的核心在於探討民主黨內部對於醫療改革路徑的分歧，從支持「全民健保」（Medicare for All）的左翼到支持「漸進式改革」（incremental reform）的中間派，呈現了黨內的緊張關係。選項 A 錯誤，因為黨內對改革方式有嚴重分歧；選項 B 是黨內左翼的觀點，而非文章的客觀總結；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章強調的是民主黨內部的辯論，而非僅限於共和黨法案。
